title: Ask HN: Is MCP's real moat now adoption?
summary:
MCP was pitched as a fix for M*N integration problem, expose your data and tools through MCP once, and any compatible agent can use them.

Two things have since kinda changed?

1. An agent can now lookup APIs, documentation and call APIs on the fly. 2. MCP's scaling problem seems to have undercut its original promise. If you connect too many servers - it eats up context, so tool loading is deferred or the agent generates code to call a tool, and we are back to square one.

I think the best argument is adoption and a bunch of benefits fall out of that - standard auth, API gateway, credential management, all of which could have been done just as well or better, but MCP seems to have won purely because of adoption?

What did I miss?

title: Ask HN: In the age of agentic AI, do you still pair program?
summary:
What about mob/ensemble programming? I work on a team that used to use mob programming heavily. There would be a driver and a navigator, and then someone taking notes. Other people would be "muses" or observers. Always occurring over Zoom. I always felt like this was a very draining way of programming. Pair programming felt a bit better. Of course, we still get together to discuss architecture or how we want to go about a certain set of work or if we're blocked, but with agents, it just doesn't make sense to get everybody in a call to watch someone else's agent work.

So, in the age of agentic AI, how do these two concepts evolve (or disappear)?

title: Feedback requested on possible scam employer
summary:
I've spent the last year thinking, with growing concern, that my current company is some sort of scam. They're owned by private equity and behave in a very anti-consumer and anti-employee way. The quality of their product has deteriorated greatly, yet senior management show no signs of caring. There appears to be a plan in motion that negates all of this. Their 'technical issues' cause problems with payment providers constantly, to the point where Stripe and Mastercard may block them.

Today I figured out that they have been hiring Mormons solely for senior leadership roles. The last few new hires have been deeply unqualified for the roles but all have the Church of LDS in common. Would you hire people with degrees outside of tech for senior IT and engineering roles? Only if there were part of your specific cult. Most roles they don't even advertise, just some new dude shows up one day. And has ties with existing management. The few jobs they do post, which may be a legality, show the location as Salt Lake city even though we have no office there. Seems to be a way to target a specific type of person.

Not sure what to do with this. Are they doing anything illegal? Likely not, but I question their practices. Are they so inept and uncaring that they are a nightmare to do business with or work for? Yes.

On the plus side, it's all falling apart for them. We'll all be out of jobs soon enough. Thoughts?

title: Ask HN: How to contact Google support after cancel a subscription?
summary:
I understand this is on me for "trusting big G." Even after I've de-Googled my life as much as I could, I wanted to give their Antigravity CLI offering a shot.

So I made a new account using my own domain and subscribed to Google One using my credit card. Even after getting access to Google One, I was not allowed to use Antigravity due to "verification purposes." After a very hostile verification process and adding a brand-new `@gmail.com` address to this same account, I could finally use Antigravity.

After the 3 months at a discount ended, I decided I didn't like Antigravity's capabilities, so I canceled my Google One subscription, deleted everything, and didn't think about it anymore. But I've just been charged for it! I logged back in, and the subscription doesn't show as active.

However, I did have PayPal as my payment method, which I added after adding the `@gmail.com` address. This method was NOT the one used to charge my credit card, though. I still removed it for safety.

So my theory is that I successfully created my account and subscription (with my personal domain), and this is the subscription that stays active. But once I added the Gmail address, they didn't fully migrate my subscription, so it's a "zombie" subscription.

I've tried to log in with my personal domain email, but they say the account doesn't exist.

I've also tried to contact support, but since I'm not a "paying subscriber" anymore (even though they're charging me), I can't get in touch with a real person.

How could I fix this? I know the easiest action would be to request a chargeback through my bank, but I've read a lot of horror stories about getting "nuked" by Google if that ever happens. Even though I barely use Google anymore, I do have a very old account with them that I probably can't migrate away from.

Thank you!
